NVIDIA INTERVENTION PRECEDED HALT OF US CHIP SMUGGLING PROBE

A US Commerce Department investigation into suspected Nvidia ($NVDA ) chip smuggling to China was halted and transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia's legal team contacted investigators, according to The New York Times.

Nvidia's general counsel reportedly cited authorization from a senior Commerce official, raising concerns among investigators about potential interference.

The case involves Megaspeed, whose former executive has been accused by US officials of links to Chinese intelligence.

posts.author: The Kobeissi Letter
posts.text:
The scale of Big Tech's AI future financial obligations is extraordinary:

Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Anthropic, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, Oracle, $ORCL, and Nvidia, $NVDA, have disclosed a combined $4.49 trillion in off-balance-sheet obligations.

These include future lease payments that have not yet commenced, data-center commitments, equipment purchases, and other contractual obligations.

Alphabet accounts for the largest amount, at $1.08 trillion, followed by Anthropic, at $865 billion, and Meta, at $810 billion.

By comparison, their combined on-balance-sheet obligations total just $758 billion, consisting of long-term debt and existing lease liabilities.

This means off-balance-sheet commitments are nearly 6 times larger than their on-balance-sheet obligations.

In total, these 7 tech companies face ~$5.25 trillion in combined financial obligations.

The AI infrastructure race is facing enormous future financial commitments.

FED'S BARKIN WARNS INFLATION RISKS REMAIN ELEVATED

Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin says inflation remains the primary risk to the Federal Reserve's dual mandate, calling for monetary policy to move carefully.

Barkin describes the US economy as “remarkably stable,” with resilient consumer spending, strong corporate earnings and healthy lending demand.

However, businesses report broad-based cost pressures and plans to pass higher expenses on to consumers.

Layoffs remain muted despite weak consumer sentiment.

EVEN A SMALL CPI BEAT COULD SEAL DECEMBER FED RATE HIKE

Russell Investments warns that even a modest upside surprise in Tuesday's US CPI report could cement a December Fed rate hike.

Following strong employment data and signs of economic resilience, strategist BeiChen Lin expects the Fed to have little tolerance for persistent inflation.

Markets now price an 84.5% probability of a 25-basis-point hike on December 9, up from 76.3% a day earlier

US OCTOBER CPI REPORT TO OMIT ANNUAL INFLATION FIGURES

The Bureau of Labor Statistics will exclude year-over-year headline and core CPI figures from Tuesday's October inflation report.

Missing October 2025 price data from last year's government shutdown prevents reliable annual comparisons. Annual real earnings growth will also be unavailable.

Monthly inflation figures will still be released.

Economists expect headline CPI to rise 0.3% MoM and core CPI to increase 0.2% MoM.
